summary: The candidate is correct as stated. The realization hypothesis supplies lattice-convex positive support and the midpoint log-concavity needed for the parity and reflected-Hellinger argument. The face-restricted exponential tilt proves the entropy identity even when the ambient infimum is not attained. The finite-label fourth-moment estimate, the single application of the accepted continuous Grunbaum inequality to each whole product fiber, and the likelihood-ratio truncation establish the quantitative lower bound at points selected independently of the factor count and halfspace. Vertical halfspaces give the matching exponential upper bound, including zero-volume fibers. The strict nonvertex inequality justifies the heavy-atom critical case; the stated prefactor and eventual threshold follow with their exact constants. The finite-collection extension uses a uniform minimum positive tilted probability and correctly controls total variance by total exponential slack. Singleton and lower-rank supports, vertex and boundary tilts, zero variance, and varying continuous dimensions are all covered without a gap.
